reasons: Lake identity confirms Camara v. Municipal Court, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 1967-06-05, year 1967.
Lake citations list official 387 U.S. 523, parallels 87 S. Ct. 1727 and 18 L. Ed. 2d 930, and vendor-neutral 1967 U.S. LEXIS 1254.
The opinion is centrally about administrative inspection/search programs and warrant procedure.
Lake scope note calls Camara the foundational administrative-warrant case, supporting Key — Anchor placement for Administrative Searches.
residual_risks: No separate home-page taxonomy file was disclosed, so the Special Needs half of the combined home title is not independently tested.

defect.evidence_quote: we hold that administrative searches of the kind at issue here are significant intrusions upon the interests protected by the Fourth Amendment
defect.locator_note: content_page.md frontmatter holding; supporting limits appear in the cached opinion at pages 534, 538, and 539-540.
defect.problem: The holding is directionally supported but too broad and truncated. Camara speaks to routine code-enforcement/area-inspection searches of the kind before the Court, with consent, emergency, and timing limits; "area warrant" is shorthand rather than the Court's quoted term.
defect.proposed_fix: Tighten to: Routine municipal code-enforcement inspections of private dwellings or structures require a warrant procedure after refusal and absent emergency; probable cause may rest on reasonable legislative or administrative area-inspection standards rather than individualized suspicion.

reasons: The p.534 holding is expressly limited to "administrative searches of the kind at issue here."
The p.538 passage supports reasonable legislative or administrative standards for an area inspection of a particular dwelling.
The opinion preserves warrantless emergency inspections and says warrants normally should be sought after entry is refused, so the metadata should state those limits.
residual_risks: The page body's quote/pin assertions were not separate inventory rows, but the lake marks pin-534 and pin-538 quote_fidelity as mismatch.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: State the rule as routine municipal code-enforcement inspections, after refusal and absent emergency, with probable cause based on reasonable area standards.

reasons: Lens A does not evaluate treatment or currency.
The payload mirrors disclosed lake treatment fields: good_law, as_of_content 1967-06-05, as_of_treatment 2026-06-30, migration-seed basis, no point variance, and the Frank scope note.
residual_risks: Substantive good-law and negative-treatment assessment is reserved to lens B.
